svg.text: TWO KINDS OF DONOR PANEL, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME JOB

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Discrete tactile switches on a PCB

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: — the easy case. Cut the board free, cut the matrix traces, and wire each switch: one leg

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: to the common node, the other through its resistor to ground.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: — rubber caps pressing onto interdigitated traces. Same electrical job, much fiddlier:

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: the traces are fine-pitch and they melt. Practise on a spare corner of the flexi first.

text.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif

svg.text: Either way the resistors can live on your own board rather than on the fascia — only the switch wires have to cross.
